core_phrases.irish: Cén fáth ar thug tú sin dó?
core_phrases.english: Why did you give that to him?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Cén (kayn) fáth (faw) ar (er) thug (hug) tú (too) sin (shin) dó (doh)

grammar_rule.title: Forming questions with question words
grammar_rule.explanation: Question words like 'Cad' (What), 'Cén' (Which), 'Cá' (Where), 'Conas' (How), 'Cathain' (When), 'Cén fáth' (Why) are used at the beginning of a sentence to form questions.
examples: Cén t-am é? (What time is it?)
Cá bhfuil an siopa? (Where is the shop?)

pronunciation_notes: Practice the pronunciation of 'Cad' as 'kaad' with emphasis on the 'a'.
Remember to pronounce 'Cén fáth' as 'kayn faw' with a slight pause between the words.
Pay attention to the pronunciation of 'Cathain' with the 'th' sound as in 'thin'.

mini_task.instruction: Record yourself asking and answering questions using the question words learned.
prompts: Ask a friend 'Cén t-am é?' (What time is it?)
Respond to 'Conas atá tú?' (How are you?) with 'Tá mé go maith' (I am good).
Create a dialogue using 'Cá bhfuil an siopa?' (Where is the shop?)
